Interactive D3 ridgeline chart

pv_ridgeline.Rd

Overlapping kernel density curves, one ridge per group, ordered by median from the top down — the readable way to compare the shape of a distribution across up to 8 groups. Hovering a ridge lifts it to full opacity, dims the rest, and shows the group's median and size.

Usage

pv_ridgeline(
  data,
  value,
  group,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  mode = "auto",
  duration = 600,
  source = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  elementId = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

value

Name of the numeric column whose distribution is drawn. Rows with a missing value or group are dropped with a warning.

group

Name of the grouping column (one ridge per level, max 8; every level needs at least 2 non-missing values).

xlab

X-axis title. NULL (the default) uses the value column name; NA or "" suppresses it; any other string replaces it.

ylab

Optional rotated title beside the group labels. Ridges are labelled directly, so NULL (the default) draws none, same as NA or ""; a string adds one.

title, subtitle

Optional chart heading text.

mode

"auto" (default: follow the viewer's light/dark setting), "light", or "dark".

duration

Entrance transition length in ms.

source

Optional source/credit line, shown small and grey at the bottom left — e.g. "Source: Bundesamt für Statistik".

width, height, elementId

Standard htmlwidgets sizing arguments.

Value

An htmlwidget.

Examples

pv_ridgeline(pv_fiscal, value = "resource_index", group = "year",
             title = "Resource index across municipalities")
